Year 2036. Following a months-long regional blackout and winter evacuation, an isolated knowledge repository remains powered by its sealed modular microreactor. A harsh snowstorm over a low concrete server facility, only a handful of amber windows and cooling vapor, silent antenna field, buried access road, derelict transmission pylons. Main image is distant journalist photograph from snow-covered hill, genuinely remote not giant sci-fi complex. Evidence frames: grainy CCTV in unattended server aisle; satellite thermal image locating one warm facility in the frozen dark; exhausted civilian technicians accessing an archive terminal in a school with printed manuals. Reactor only as sealed ancillary building, no interior engineering. Exact title 'THE KOLA ARCHIVE'. Subtitle '2036 / REGIONAL COLLAPSE'. Three labels 'GRID: LOST', 'ARCHIVE: ONLINE', 'RECOVERY ACCESS: OPEN'. Bottom statement 'THE REGION WENT DARK. ITS MEMORY DID NOT.'

images.title: FORREST FOR THE TREES — AFTERMATH
images.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create one stunning finished 16:9 widescreen MOSAIC fictional dystopian game loading screen. Incident: FORREST FOR THE TREES, 2035, hidden railguns in a densely packed slum have just fired and almost triggered an orbital debris cascade. Depict ONLY THE MOMENT AFTER, a deeply beautiful and horrifying silent aftermath. Main image 85 percent of composition, documentary night photograph from a nearby rooftop: dense improvised slum roofs, corrugated sheet metal, water tanks, laundry lines, dirty concrete alleys and dangling wires occupying bottom third. Several extremely long fictional railgun barrels concealed among the shacks are now exposed, aimed skyward at distinct angles, their external barrels still glowing cherry red and orange with residual heat, thin wisps of pale smoke and heat shimmer illuminating nearby rusted roofs. No firing beams or muzzle flash, no schematics or weapon internals. The sky is vast, deep midnight blue and dominates upper two thirds; dozens of delicate white-gold and pale cyan shooting-star trails are just beginning to multiply across the heavens, some fragment into branching clusters, a few brighter reentries reflected on sheet-metal roofs. Maintain huge dark negative-space between streaks so the sky remains celestial and awe inspiring, not fireworks or a laser battle. One unmistakable distant orbital fragmentation bloom is subtle, almost like a flower of light. Several tiny ordinary residents on roofs, a parent and child silhouetted beside a water tank, stare upward, entirely still. Horror conveyed through the contrast of fragile inhabited homes, ominous red cooling machinery and the beautiful expanding consequence overhead. Atmosphere contemplative, tragic, sublime, terrible beauty, no gore, no triumphant hero, no explosions at ground level. Filmic deep blacks, silver-blue starlight and warm ember glow, fine night-camera grain, realistic weathered environment, extraordinary photographic composition. Thin navy-black archival header and footer with understated white condensed typography, fine cyan rule, discreet MOSAIC WORLD ARCHIVE logo. Exact headline 'FORREST FOR THE TREES'. Exact small subtitle '2035 / THE NIGHT THE SKY BROKE'. Bottom line 'FOR A MOMENT, EVERYONE LOOKED UP.' Two SMALL peripheral evidence inset frames in a narrow bottom corner: grainy thermal CCTV showing hot barrels distributed among dense housing, and an orbital tracking monitor with a spreading scatter of dots labeled 'CASCADE WARNING'. These insets must not compete with the overwhelming night sky or cover the people. Visual storytelling comes first; minimal text. Standalone image, no screen mockup, no loading progress bar. Entirely fictional game artwork, nonfunctional external weapon props only.
